findings.claim: Magnifique kaolin clay firing claim and stovetop/oven rating vs. composition disclosure
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Magnifique markets its clayware as '100% pure kaolin clay' glazed with kaolin clay fired '>1,500°F' and rates stovetop/oven use up to 750°F (400°C) on cookmagnifique.com (excluding induction); however, Dillard's and some manual listings for the 4-Qt Casserole Claypot Multi-Cooker (MCP41P-CRCR) specify an oven-safe rating of 450°F–500°F. Cookmagnifique.com never mentions 'petalite', 'spodumene', or 'stoneware', so low-expansion additives are undisclosed. Magnifique manuals still warn against thermal shock (cold liquid/frozen food in hot pot, fridge-to-oven) and exclude thermal-shock cracking from warranty.
findings.value_or_range: Glaze firing >1,500°F (>815°C); stovetop (gas/electric) & oven rating up to 750°F (400°C), or 450–500°F on MCP41P-CRCR; petalite/spodumene/stoneware not disclosed

findings.claim: Ceramic chemistry of >1,500°F kaolin firing vs. flameware thermal-shock resistance
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Because Magnifique does not publish its full mineral batch recipe or peak bisque/glost cone, whether its body uses lithium-aluminosilicate (LAS) minerals or high-mullite/controlled-porosity stoneware fired well above 1,500°F cannot be confirmed from public disclosures. At ~1,500°F (815°C) alone, kaolin has only dehydroxylated to metakaolin (450–650°C) and passed calcination/low-fire frit milestones (~815°C), well below spinel/mullite formation (>900–1,050°C) and stoneware vitrification (1,200–1,300°C+ / Cone 6–10). Stovetop flameware normally relies on petalite or spodumene (firing 1,100–1,350°C to form beta-spodumene with CTE 0.5–2.5 × 10^-6/°C vs. 3–7 × 10^-6/°C for standard whiteware) plus matched low-expansion glazes.
findings.value_or_range: Kaolin dehydroxylation 450–650°C (842–1,202°F); calcination milestone ~815°C (1,500°F); mullite >900–1,050°C; LAS flameware firing 1,100–1,350°C (CTE 0.5–2.5 × 10^-6/°C)

findings.claim: Magnifique Slow Cook Low and High temperatures and model wattages
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Exact numeric °F/°C setpoints for Slow Cook Low and High are NOT disclosed in Magnifique manuals or cookmagnifique.com; manuals define Low (traditional ~8–10 hr slow cook) and High (faster ~4–6 hr cook; default Slow Cook state on multi-cookers requiring manual TEMP arrow toggle to Low) functionally, followed by Keep Warm (recommended max 4 hours). One single-source CNET review of a Magnifique Combo Air Fryer + Multicooker measured a 214°F ceiling on its bottom cooker (LOW CONFIDENCE for extrapolating to MCR51P/MCP41P). Wattage diverges sharply between standard Magnifique ceramic slow cookers (260–280W, 120V/60Hz) and the 4.5-Qt Clay Multi-Cooker MCR51P (1,130W, 120V/60Hz).
findings.value_or_range: Slow Cook Low/High °F undisclosed (214°F max in CNET combo review [LOW CONFIDENCE]); 260–280W (ceramic slow cookers) vs. 1,130W (MCR51P Clay Multi-Cooker)

findings.claim: VitaClay wattages for VM7900, VF7700, and VM7800 series (120V / 60Hz)
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Official manuals cover both 6-cup (3-qt) and 8-cup (4-qt) capacities under a combined 500–600W rating. Individual retail spec sheets break out VF7700-6 as 500W and VF7700-8 as 600W; VM7800-5C (6–6.5-qt stock pot) is rated 600W (or 500–600W in series overviews, 110–120 VAC / 60 Hz).

findings.claim: VitaClay VS7600-2C wattage (2-Qt Yogurt Maker & Personal Slow Cooker)
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: LOW CONFIDENCE: Multiple third-party retail spec sheets (Staples.ca, Juicers4Life, eBay, Ubuy) list VS7600-2C at 120W (120V / 60Hz), whereas vitaclaychef.com text snippets omit an explicit wattage and some secondary listings (alternate Staples.ca / Desertcart entries) copy-paste the generic 500–600W boilerplate from larger VitaClay multi-cookers. Physical unit rating label or direct PDF table inspection was not surfaced in indexed web snippets.
findings.value_or_range: 120W (retail spec sheets) vs. 500–600W (generic boilerplate listings; unconfirmed on vitaclaychef.com)

findings.claim: VitaClay double-lid / steam-vent evaporation behavior over 2–8 hour slow cooks and liquid top-up rules
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Behavior splits by model family. On VM7900 and VF7700, an inner clay lid sits beneath an outer lid with a steam vent/cap to create a micro-pressure seal that circulates condensation and cooks ~2–4× faster—converting standard 8-hr Low / 4-hr High slow-cooker recipes to ~2 hours on Soup/Stew, minimizing liquid loss so 6–8 hr cycles are generally unnecessary (check halfway on first use). By contrast, VM7800 (VM7800-5C clay high-dome lid / VM7800-5S stoneware dome lid) is explicitly documented by vitaclaychef.com to evaporate liquid more quickly like a stovetop stockpot: for cycles >1 hour (e.g., 4–8 hr bone broths), VitaClay requires 4–8 cups starting liquid (up to 8 cups/hr on long cycles), periodic monitoring, and topping up with warm or room-temperature liquid only (never cold liquid into a hot pot, and never dry-cooking).
findings.value_or_range: VM7900/VF7700: ~2 hr equivalent for 8-hr crockpot recipes (minimal evaporation; warm top-up only if needed); VM7800 stock pot: faster evaporation, 4–8 cups baseline liquid, periodic warm/room-temp top-ups required for multi-hour cooks

findings.claim: VitaClay 480°F thermal shock resistance claim presence outside one YouTube video
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Refutes the premise that it only appears in one YouTube video: the verbatim claim 'High-fired clay pot with wider temperature shock resistance up to 480 F that enhances longevity.' appears directly on official vitaclaychef.com product pages (including VM7900 listings) in addition to YouTube video descriptions. However, '480°F' / '480 F' does NOT appear in indexed VitaClay PDF instruction manuals (ManualsLib, Home Depot thdstatic.com, media-amazon.com), which instead provide qualitative thermal-shock warnings and explicitly prohibit stovetop, oven, and broiler use.
findings.value_or_range: 480°F (verbatim on vitaclaychef.com web pages and YouTube; absent from indexed PDF manuals)

myths_checked: Myth: VitaClay's 480°F thermal shock claim appears only in a single YouTube video. Checked: False — the verbatim line 'High-fired clay pot with wider temperature shock resistance up to 480 F that enhances longevity.' is published on official vitaclaychef.com product pages as well as YouTube, though absent from PDF user manuals and not an oven/stovetop rating.

Myth: Magnifique discloses petalite or spodumene flameware chemistry to explain its >1,500°F firing and 750°F stovetop/oven rating. Checked: False — 'petalite', 'spodumene', and 'stoneware' do not appear on cookmagnifique.com; Magnifique discloses only '100% pure kaolin clay' and kaolin glaze fired >1,500°F without naming low-expansion lithium additives.

Myth: All VitaClay cookers share identical 500–600W ratings and identical no-evaporation double-lid behavior over 2–8 hours. Checked: False — VM7800 stock pots evaporate significantly faster than VM7900/VF7700 double-lid units and require periodic liquid monitoring/warm top-ups over multi-hour cooks, while the 2-qt VS7600-2C is listed at 120W on multiple retail spec sheets (versus 500–600W boilerplate).
